To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
vein formation in the Ouachita mountains was dominated by diffusion and advection, and was not a purely diffusion-dominated process.

the stable isotope compositions of veins and their host rocks are controlled by fluid-rock interaction processes and that diffusion and advection are both important mechanisms for transporting 18O and other elements during vein formation.

the stable isotope compositions of vein quartz and vein calcite reflect those of the host rock, and the degree of isotopic exchange between vein and host rock is dependent on the permeability of the host rock.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of diffusion, advector, and lithologic control on fluid-rock interaction and vein formation.
the importance of fluid-rock interaction processes during vein formation and the role of diffusion, adivation, and rock lithology in controlling these processes.
the role of host-rock composition and lithology on the formation of vein minerals and the mass-transport mechanisms that are important in vein formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diffusion, advection and rock lithology were all important in vein formation in the Paleozoic of the Ouachita Orogenic belt.

the δ18O and δ13C values of quartz and calcite in veins formed during regional deformation and low-grade metamorphism are strongly controlled by the host-rock composition, and that diffusion and advection are important processes in vein formation.
vein formation in the Ouachita belt was controlled by a combination of diffusion, ad-vection, and host rock lithology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
vein formation is controlled by diffusion and advection in a rock-buffered hydrothermal system.

diffusion, advection and rock lithology all play an important role in vein formation, and the relative contribution of each depends on the local rock type, the vein geometry, and the vein orientation.
vein formation is controlled by the relative rates of advection and diffusion and the lithology of the host rocks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

diffusion and advection are important processes for the transport of 18O and C into veins, and the degree of diffusion or advection depends on lithology, vein orientation, and the distance from the source of fluid.

the oxygen isotope composition of vein quartz is not a good proxy for the temperature of vein formation, and that it is important to consider the effects of diffusion, advention, and lithology on vein composition.
diffusion and advection, in addition to fluid-rock interaction, play an important role in determining the stable isotope compositions of vein quartz, vein calcite, and host-rock minerals.
